summary: Ryoichi Kondo (1930–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. By 2026, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and under Manshi Kiyozawa at Kōkōdō. He taught at Toyo University (1916–1924) and held professorships and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi (1926–2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor of literature at Otani University (attested 1978, 1993).
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2020–2026).
Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo until 1963. She served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Ryukoku University (1897), the Third Higher School (from 1899), and served as a professor at Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. He served as professor (1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012), and director at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (ca. 1971–1980). He became a professor at Hanazono University around 1993 and served as a staff member at the Research Institute of Soto Studies.

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He served as a professor (from 1975), dean of literature (1981), and professor emeritus (1990–1994) at Taisho University.

Ryosho Nakamura (born 1927) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Ensho Kanakura at Tohoku University and later earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He served as a professor at Kagoshima International University from circa 1965 to 1998.
Ryōshō Taira (1906–1985) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who was attested as a professor emeritus at Taisho University in 1976 and held a post there in 1984.

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions at Komazawa from assistant (1962) to professor (1964), dean (1991), and president (2009), and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1998) and at the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Otani University, where he later held a post from circa 1935 to 1969, before serving as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (ca. 1969–1984).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (ca. 1942–1947) and later served as professor emeritus there from circa 1972 to 1992.

Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Waseda University. He became a professor there around 2004, and also held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryosuke Furui (born 1971) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007. He joined the University of Tokyo, where he is attested as a professor by 2026.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University (attested 2015). He also held a research post at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015).
